title: On the existence of a morphism between certain Artin-Schreier curves
summary: It is well known that, given two curves $\mathcal{X}: y^p+cy=x^m$ and $\mathcal{Y}:y^p+cy=x^n$, defined over $\F_p$, if $n$ divides $m$ then there exists a nonconstant morphism $\mathcal{X} \longrightarrow \mathcal{Y}$. In this paper we are interested in studying whether the converse of this statement is true, i.e., if there exists a morphism $\mathcal{X} \longrightarrow\mathcal{Y}$ then must it be true that $n$ divides $m$?
